In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a given laser system and a given set of experimental conditions, it is possible to design a dielectric multilayer mirror which will produce negligible dispersion.
the use of lambda/4 dielectric mirrors in mode locked laser cavities is not advisable.
the use of lambda/4 dielectric mirrors in mode locked dye lasers is not recommended, unless the dispersion is compensated for by the use of a prism or grating.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of dielectric mirrors in femtosecdon dye lasers can be very beneficial if the dispersion is carefully considered and controlled.
the dispersion of a lambda/4 dielectric mirror can be reduced to a negligible value if the thickness of the layers are kept small.
the dispersion of the dielectric multilayer mirrors should be carefully considered in the design of the mode locked cavity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amount of dispersion introduced by a dielectric mirror is not a constant but rather it is a function of the laser wavelength, the mirror reflectivity and the mirror construction parameters.
the dispersion of the dielectric mirror is not negligible, even for the case of a 3 layer mirror, and it is not linear with the number of layers.

the amount of dispersion can easily be reduced by using a dielectric mirror with a smaller number of layers, or by using a dielectirc mirror with a larger wavelength of the first order reflection maximum.
